title: One kindness
tomorrow: Paul says examine yourselves. he also says he won't. which?

segments.voice: Yesterday, arrow prayers again, short and aimed: all day, short. Today the aim turns outward, toward one person.

At some memorials, people line up at a microphone to tell stories. In Acts, at Joppa, nobody gives a speech at all. A disciple named Tabitha, also called Dorcas, has died, and her friends send for Peter. When he comes into the upper room, the widows stand around him weeping, “shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.” Why coats? Why not a eulogy?
screen: `A LINE AT THE MICROPHONE.` → `IN JOPPA, NO SPEECH.` → `WHY COATS?`

segments.voice: Acts gives her one line of description: “this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.” Then, instead of explaining, it shows. A coat, then another, held up one at a time. That's the solve. Each garment was made for somebody in particular, and each widow is holding hers. Dorcas's goodness wasn't a mood spread thin over everyone. It came one coat at a time, each with a name on it. Peter sends everyone out, kneels and prays, and she opens her eyes. But before the miracle, the story lingers on the pile of clothes. Jesus sets the bar low on purpose. In Matthew, whoever gives “a cup of cold water only” to one of his little ones won't lose the reward. A cup of water. Only. And Ephesians puts it plainly: “be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another.” Thérèse of Lisieux, from earlier this year, called her path the little way and wrote about small, hidden kindnesses in an ordinary day. So one kindness means one deliberate act, chosen on purpose, for one person. Something to tell a friend tonight: Acts remembers Dorcas with a pile of coats, not a speech.
screen: `FULL OF GOOD WORKS.` · `ONE COAT AT A TIME.` · `A CUP OF COLD WATER ONLY.` · `THE LITTLE WAY.` · then, large: `ONE A DAY.`

segments.voice: Pick up your phone and bring one person to mind who could use something small today. Send them one specific kindness, not a general hello: thanks for something exact, an offer of one concrete thing, a memory they'd smile at. If you pray, hold their name for a moment as it sends.
One kindness. One deliberate act, for one person, chosen on purpose, the way Dorcas made one coat at a time.
The line to keep: one a day, a coat at a time, each with a name on it. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Christians choose one deliberate kindness each day, often small and unseen, as a way of following Jesus, and some church groups still sew and knit clothing for people in need.

chat.says: Pop snapped at me for carrying his plate. i've been helping with EVERYTHING since the doctor. too much??
options: Maybe. Ask what one thing he'd really want. One aimed kindness, not all of it.
Keep going. Kindness can't be overdone, and he'll thank you for it later.
Back off completely. If he wants help, he can ask for it himself.
chat.meaning: Dorcas's kindness came one coat at a time, each for a particular person. One deliberate kindness fits the person; help spread over everything can smother.
